claim: In the matching retail DLL, instance uAudio.uAudioPlayer.Play (0x060052E7) has source-audited RVA 0x00325A80, exact signature blob 20010115118839011182c1, one System.Nullable<System.TimeSpan> parameter startOff, and an exact 564-byte code body. Raw State==1 returns immediately; raw State==2 calls sibling Pause (0x060052E9) and returns. Otherwise it writes State=1, SongDone=false and flare_SongEnd=false, then writes get_UAudio().targetFile=this.targetFile. When myAudioSource.clip is null it attempts get_UAudio().LoadMainOutputStream(); on success it builds a PCMReaderCallback from this plus ldftn Song_Stream_Loop (0x060052E8), opens targetFile, replaces readFullyStream with a ReadFullyStream whose stream_CanSeek is true, constructs NLayer.MpegFile(readFullyStream,true), conditionally performs an initial ReadSamples when startOff has a value equal to TimeSpan.Zero, stores that MpegFile to playbackDevice, obtains get_UAudio().SongLength, clamps it to Int32.MaxValue, and creates streaming AudioClip literal 'uAudio_song' using the MpegFile WaveFormat channels/sample-rate and the callback. It assigns the clip, sets loop=true and timeSamples=0, then calls set_CurrentTime(TimeSpan.Zero) when startOff has no value or set_CurrentTime(startOff.Value) otherwise. Inside a nested System.Object catch it conditionally invokes get_sendPlaybackState() with raw 1. If LoadMainOutputStream was false it writes myAudioSource.clip=null. The shared tail checks myAudioSource.clip != null; when non-null it calls AudioSource.Play only if not already playing and then writes updateTime=true, otherwise it writes State=0. A surrounding System.Exception catch also writes State=0. The method has exactly two fat EH clauses. FACT-0133 pins the two already-canonical caller sites at Menu_SoundManager.MyMusic_Play IL+0x00F6 and IL+0x01AD.
